word-resume.def: a short document listing your education, jobs and skills that you send when applying for work

word-vacancy.def: a position at a company that is open and needs someone to fill it

word-job-offer.def: a company's formal proposal to hire you, usually with a salary and a start date

word-full-time.def: working the whole normal week, usually about forty hours

word-part-time.def: working fewer hours than the normal week requires

word-overtime.def: extra hours worked beyond the normal schedule, often paid at a higher rate

word-sick-leave.def: days away from your workplace because you are ill, often still paid

word-maternity-leave.def: a period away from your workplace for a mother before and after having a baby

word-resign.def: to tell your employer that you are leaving your position by your own choice

word-retire.def: to stop working permanently, usually because you have reached an older age

word-promotion.def: a move to a more senior position at your company

word-pay-raise.def: an increase in the regular amount of money you earn

word-bonus.def: extra money given on top of your normal earnings, for example for good results

word-qualification.def: a degree, exam result or skill that makes you suitable for a certain position

word-staff.def: all the people who are hired by a company or organization

word-department.def: one section of a large company, school or government, with its own task

word-workplace.def: the building or room where you do your job

word-presentation.def: a talk in which you show information to a group, often with slides

word-report-n.def: a document that gives facts and findings about a subject

word-conference.def: a large formal meeting where people discuss a topic, often for several days

word-business-trip.def: a journey you make for your employer instead of for vacation

word-client.def: a person or company that pays a professional for a service

word-trade-union.def: an organization of workers that protects their rights, pay and conditions

word-strike.def: a refusal by workers to do their jobs, as a protest about pay or conditions

word-unemployment.def: the state of having no paid occupation although you want one

word-job-center.def: a government office that helps people find a new position

word-freelancer.def: a person who does tasks for several clients without being hired by one company

word-self-employed.def: earning money from your own business instead of from a boss

word-entrepreneur.def: a person who starts a new business and takes financial risks

word-intern.def: a student or beginner who works for a short period to gain experience

word-remote-work.def: doing your tasks from home or any place outside the office

word-feierabend.gl: Feierabend: German for the end of the workday and the free time after it
